rfi.title: France faces record €340bn borrowing test as government braces for 2027 budget
rfi.description: France has announced plans to borrow a record amount on the bond market next year, days before the government unveils its 2027 budget this Thursday. As the country's debt hits its highest level in 80 years and investors up their rates, ministers are under pressure to slash spending – yet surging inflation, strikes and approaching elections are setting the stage for a tussle in parliament over proposed cuts.

rfi.title: Who is Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, Morocco’s first female prime minister?
rfi.description: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri has been named Morocco’s first female prime minister – another first for the 50-year-old lawyer, who became the first female mayor of Marrakesh 17 years ago. But who is the woman now tasked with leading Morocco’s government?

rfi.title: ‘Welcome back’: Macron and Sanchez embrace prospect of UK return to EU
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has welcomed British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's reopening of the debate over the United Kingdom's relationship with the European Union, responding to the possibility of the UK eventually rejoining the bloc with a simple message in English: “Welcome back.”

rfi.title: Exiled Burkina publisher tells RFI of repression and fear four years after coup
rfi.description: Burkina Faso on Wednesday marks four years since military strongman Captain Ibrahim Traoré took over in a coup. Comparing himself to anti-colonial icon Thomas Sankara, Traoré promised a "progressive and popular" revolution. RFI spoke to Inoussa Ouédraogo, a publishing director who now lives in exile about the country's fading human rights record.

rfi.title: Mali army and Russian fighters accused of killing dozens of civilians
rfi.description: Mali’s armed forces and Russian Wagner Group personnel committed war crimes including killings and torture of civilians during joint operations between 2023 and 2025, Amnesty International has said in a new report documenting abuses across several regions of the country.

rfi.title: US troops wrap up Iraq mission 12 years after Islamic State offensive
rfi.description: Iraq is closing a major chapter in its post-2003 history as the US-led coalition against Islamic State ends its mission – more than two decades after France opposed the invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein.

rfi.title: Eiffel Tower chief to leave after women sidelined during Hindu visit
rfi.description: Eiffel Tower director Patrick Branco Ruivo will step down at the end of the year, the tower’s operator has announced, after female staff were excluded during a visit by a Hindu religious group – an incident that triggered a strike that closed the Paris landmark for a day.

rfi.title: Rugby World Cup bosses promise big party at first 24-team tournament
rfi.description: Organisers of the 2027 Rugby World Cup on Wednesday promised a massive party during the first 24-team tournament, which starts next October in Perth, Western Australia.

rfi.title: US Supreme Court lifts limits on third-country deportations
rfi.description: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday lifted restrictions on the deportations of immigrants to countries that are not their own, while agreeing to hear the issue on its merits in December.

rfi.title: Heatwaves and wildfires drive extreme ozone pollution worldwide
rfi.description: Heatwaves, wildfires and human-caused emissions exposed a third of the world’s population to extremely high ozone pollution in 2026, with Asia worst hit and wildfire smoke crossing oceans, an EU report said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Le Pen ally Bardella sues over antisemitism claims, alleges 'total war'
rfi.description: Jordan Bardella, a key ally of French far-right presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, on Tuesday said allegations he made antisemitic comments in 2013 marked part of a "total war" against their National Rally party ahead of the 2027 polls. Backed by fellow party members, Bardella announced that he had filed a complaint for defamation.

rfi.title: Ghana boss Queiroz refuses to quit after poor start to 2027 AFCON qualifiers
rfi.description: Ghana head coach Carlos Queiroz on Wednesday refused to resign after his side's calamitous 4-2 defeat at home to Gambia in qualifiers for next year's Africa Cup of Nations in Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda.

rfi.title: French PM warns against student violence as public sector strike kicks off
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has warned against an escalation of the demonstrations in secondary schools, which have broken out ahead of a nationwide strike by public-sector workers. More than 100 pupils were arrested on Monday during violent clashes with police. It comes amid mounting anger over the national budget, which is due to be unveiled on Thursday.

rfi.title: French public sector workers strike over pay freeze ahead of 2027 budget
rfi.description: Teachers, healthcare workers, local government staff, tax officials and firefighters in France are on strike Tuesday to pressure the government ahead of the 2027 budget debates which could see public sector salaries frozen for a fourth straight year.

rfi.title: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger launch Tafouk TV channel to push their own narrative
rfi.description: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are stepping up their joint media push with Tafouk TV, a new television channel aimed at challenging Western coverage and promoting the three military-led Sahel states’ own account of events.

rfi.title: French prosecutors seek 'severe' punishment for ex-minister Dati in graft case
rfi.description: France prosecutors on Monday sought two years with an electronic tag and a five-year ban on public office for ex-culture minister Rachida Dati in a trial on corruption charges linked to dealings with the Renault-Nissan group. Her lawyers have slammed the severity of the recommendations which will be announced in January next year.

rfi.title: US has 'alienated' Sudan's army in 'complex war' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has vowed to push on with his fight against the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, despite a US visa snub to attend the UN General Assembly and mounting pressure for a ceasefire. RFI spoke to a Sudanese researcher about why such a step was taken and how far the stand-off could go.

rfi.title: Egypt, Senegal and Ghana face pressure to relaunch drive for 2027 AFCON
rfi.description: Continental powerhouses Egypt, Ghana and Senegal will attempt to get their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaigns back on track on Tuesday after opening round setbacks last week.

lemonde.description: Des actions ont eu lieu dans des établissements en Ile-de-France, à Lyon, Strasbourg ou Nice, le principal syndicat appelant à une poursuite de la mobilisation et à une rencontre avec le ministre de l’éducation. Ce dernier a annoncé que 119 élèves et personnels ont été blessés depuis le début du mouvement.

lemonde.title: Emmanuel Macron juge les propos antisémites imputés à Jordan Bardella « gravissimes et inacceptables » ; le président du RN lui répond
lemonde.description: Le chef de l’Etat a réagi, de Madrid, à l’enquête de « Mediapart » qui rapporte des propos antisémites de Jordan Bardella lorsqu’il était jeune militant du FN. « Après le 7 octobre 2023, j’ai marché dans les rues de Paris, et me suis rendu en Israël. Pas lui », a réagi le président du RN.

lemonde.title: Guerre en Ukraine : une nouvelle demande d’aide financière qui passe mal à Bruxelles
lemonde.description: Alors que l’UE commence à débourser 90 milliards d’euros pour soutenir Kiev d’ici à la fin de 2027, l’Ukraine demande déjà une rallonge de plusieurs dizaines de milliards d’euros. L’Europe cherche des solutions et pourrait devoir rouvrir le débat sur l’utilisation des avoirs russes immobilisés sur le Vieux Continent.

lemonde.title: Après la tentative de détournement d’un avion de Flydubai volant vers Tel-Aviv, des témoignages et des zones d’ombre
lemonde.description: Le vol, parti de Dubaï, a atterri mercredi en urgence en Arabie saoudite, après qu’un des pilotes a poignardé l’autre. Les autorités israéliennes n’excluent ni une attaque terroriste ni un geste suicidaire. Benyamin Nétanyahou avait mis en garde, la veille, contre des attaques éventuelles avant les élections législatives prévues pour le 27 octobre.

lemonde.title: Budget de la Sécurité sociale : les conséquences redoutées d’une absence de vote à l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Dans une Assemblée sans majorité, l’approbation du PLFSS pour 2027 semble très incertaine. En cas de blocage, la « Sécu » continuerait à verser les prestations, mais au prix d’une dégradation des comptes sociaux et d’un flou pour le secteur hospitalier et les industries pharmaceutiques.

lemonde.title: Interpellation violente à Corbeil-Essonnes : la nouvelle vidéo qui contredit la version des policiers
lemonde.description: Les images saisies par une deuxième caméra-piéton lors d’un contrôle de police qui a dégénéré, le 5 novembre 2024, dans le quartier de Montconseil, à Corbeil-Essonnes, démontrent, selon l’IGPN, « que les faits ne s[e so]nt pas déroulés tels qu’ils [o]nt été relatés par le gardien de la paix dans le procès-verbal ».

lemonde.description: Alors qu’il affirmait vouloir réduire les émissions de méthane liées au secteur des énergies fossiles, Emmanuel Macron a finalement plaidé pour reporter l’entrée en vigueur d’une législation européenne sur le sujet, au nom de la crise énergétique.

lemonde.title: « Le danger des épisodes méditerranéens », comme celui qui touche le Sud-Est actuellement, « ce sont les crues éclair : tout déborde très vite »

lemonde.title: Affaire Epstein : la diplomatie norvégienne sur le gril
lemonde.description: Les documents publiés en janvier par la Maison Blanche avaient révélé des liens entre des diplomates norvégiens et le prédateur sexuel. A Oslo, onze anciens ministres des affaires étrangères sont auditionnés au Parlement depuis mercredi.

lemonde.title: Ce que risque Manchester City après avoir enfreint les règles financières de la Premier League
lemonde.description: Retrait de points, relégation, titres annulés… Reconnu coupable de « graves violations des règles financières » du championnat anglais de football entre 2009 et 2018, le club est sous la menace de sanctions qui pourraient affecter sa saison actuelle et ses résultats passés.

france24fr.title: Blocages des lycées : la mobilisation se poursuit
france24fr.description: En France, le blocage des lycées pour revendiquer de meilleures conditions d'apprentissage se poursuit, l'Union syndicale lycéenne annonce un "acte deux" pour la journée du 6 octobre. Les bilans officiels font état de 119 élèves ou personnels blessés et 625 interpellations depuis le début du mouvement lycéen. Récit de Florent Rodo.

france24fr.title: Au Cameroun, la grève illimitée du Syndicat national des enseignants du supérieur se poursuit
france24fr.description: Au Cameroun, la rentrée universitaire prévue le 7 octobre prochain, pourrait ne pas avoir lieu. En cause, une grève illimitée déclenchée par le SYNES, le Syndicat national des enseignants du supérieur, depuis le 3 septembre 2026. Les enseignants réclament le paiement de 16 milliards de francs CFA de primes académiques , soit près de 24 million d'euros.

france24fr.title: Fin de partie pour Ronaldo, qui quitte le rassemblement de l'équipe du Portugal
france24fr.description: À 41 ans, Cristiano Ronaldo a annoncé mercredi avoir quitté le rassemblement de l'équipe du Portugal. Il promet d'expliquer "en temps voulu" les motifs de sa décision.

france24fr.title: Projet d'attaque à Fairford : "Tout porte à ⁠croire que l'Iran a joué un rôle", affirme Andy Burnham
france24fr.description: Dans une interview accordée à la BBC mercredi, le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham a indiqué avoir de "solides indications" ​que l'Iran est impliqué dans le projet présumé d'attaque ​contre la base militaire de Fairford, dans l'ouest de l'Angleterre. Téhéran a nié toute implication dans ce projet présumé d'attaque ‌contre cette base employée par l'armée de l'air américaine.

france24fr.title: Irak, une nouvelle ère ?
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis quittent définitivement l’Irak et mettent fin à une présence militaire qui avait commencé en 2003, avec le renversement de Saddam Hussein. Les forces militaires américaines s’étaient retirées d’Irak en 2011, avant d’y revenir en 2014 pour lutter contre le groupe État islamique. L’Irak salue l’ouverture d’une nouvelle ère de "souveraineté". Ce retrait s’effectue dans un contexte de guerre avec l’Iran et d’embrasement au Yémen.

france24fr.title: Où va le Burkina Faso 4 ans après le coup d'État d'Ibrahim Traoré ?
france24fr.description: 🇧🇫 Quatre ans après son arrivée au pouvoir par un putsch, Ibrahim Traoré dirige toujours le Burkina Faso. Face à l’insécurité et à la restriction de l’espace politique, une question demeure : quand prendra fin la transition ?

france24fr.title: Aux États-Unis, la condamnation à mort imminente de Christa Pike suspendue au dernier moment
france24fr.description: Christa Pike devait être exécutée par injection létale mercredi dans l'État du Tennessee, mais la cour d'appel a suspendu in extremis sa condamnation à mort, afin d'examiner la recevabilité d'un recours produit par la défense. Christa Pike avait été condamnée à la peine capitale en 1996, pour le meurtre de sa camarade Colleen Slemmer.

france24fr.title: Le Royaume-Uni met un terme à l'accord d'échange de migrants avec la France
france24fr.description: Londres a mis fin mercredi à l'accord d'échange de migrants conclu avec Paris en 2025 pour un an. La France a indiqué discuter avec les autorités britanniques des "modalités de sortie de l'accord".

france24fr.title: Corée du Sud : derrière le succès de la K-Beauty, une forte pression sociale
france24fr.description: En Corée du Sud, la quête de beauté est devenue un véritable phénomène de société. À Séoul, les cliniques esthétiques se multiplient et les injections sont devenues courantes, sur fond de forte pression sociale autour de l’apparence. Une culture de la beauté qui nourrit aussi une industrie florissante : la K-Beauty a généré près de 10 milliards d’euros d’exportations en 2025.

france24fr.title: Vol Flydubai dérouté vers l’Arabie saoudite, la piste "terroriste" évoquée
france24fr.description:
Vol #Flydubai : ce mercredi, un avion reliant Dubaï à Tel-Aviv a été dérouté vers l’Arabie saoudite après un incident à bord.
 
Selon des témoins, l’un des pilotes aurait tenté de poignarder l’autre avec un couteau et de faire s’écraser l’appareil. Le Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu a évoqué une tentative d’attaque et a ordonné des préparatifs contre toute autre "menace potentielle" après cette tentative de détournement, tandis que le ministre de la Défense a avancé la piste d’un a

france24fr.title: Kenya : l’ambition d’autosuffisance pétrolière se heurte aux contestations
france24fr.description: Le Kenya lance la construction d’une méga-raffinerie de pétrole de 16 milliards de dollars, présentée comme un pas vers l’autosuffisance énergétique de l’Afrique. Le projet, porté par le milliardaire nigérian Aliko Dangote, doit produire jusqu’à 700 000 barils par jour et être achevé en 30 mois. Mais 133 membres d’une communauté voisine ont saisi la justice, dénonçant des risques pour l’environnement et des atteintes à leurs droits fonciers et à leur patrimoine ancestral.

france24fr.title: Irak : la coalition antijihadiste des États-Unis se retire
france24fr.description: Déployées depuis plus d'une décennie en Irak pour combattre le groupe Etat islamique (EI), les dernières troupes de la coalition antijihadiste menée par les Etats-Unis ont quitté le pays mercredi, laissant les Kurdes dans l'inquiétude.

france24fr.title: "Le Burkina est en train de devenir la nouvelle Corée du nord"
france24fr.description: Quatre ans après la prise de pouvoir du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, où va le pays des hommes intègres ? Entre menaces djihadistes et opposition bâillonnée, le journaliste en exil Newton Ahmed Barry estime qu'en concentrant le pouvoir, le dirigeant s'éloigne de l'héritage de Thomas Sankara.

france24fr.title: Un "costard en Kevlar" pour Mediapart ? La classe politique française déplore "la violence du RN"
france24fr.description: Les réactions politiques se multiplient après que Marine Le Pen a conseillé à Mediapart d'enfiler son "costard en Kevlar" – matière utilisée pour les gilets pare-balles –, à la suite de l'enquête du site d'investigation concernant des propos antisémites attribués à Jordan Bardella. Emmanuel Macron a fustigé mercredi "la violence langagière" du RN.

france24fr.title: Espagne : "la visite d'E. Macron intervient dans un contexte intérieur particulièrement troublé"
france24fr.description: La visite d’État d’Emmanuel Macron en Espagne intervient dans un contexte intérieur particulièrement troublé. Alors que le traité d’amitié et de coopération entre la France et l’Espagne, ratifié par Paris, n’a toujours pas été ratifié par Madrid — notamment en raison de l’opposition du Parti populaire, principal parti de droite face au gouvernement de Pedro Sánchez — la colère monte aussi dans le pays, notamment autour de la crise du logement. france24fr.title: Syrie: un regard exclusif sur l’intégration des combattants étrangers , l’exemple des Ouïghours
france24fr.description: Depuis le retrait américain de Syrie en avril dernier, l’armée syrienne connaît une profonde reconfiguration. Parmi les nouveaux contingents étrangers figurent quelque 2 000 combattants Ouïghours, issus du Parti islamique du Turkistan, aujourd’hui dissous. Ils constituent l’un des contingents les plus disciplinés des nouvelles forces syriennes. france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : Cyril Ramaphosa annonce des mesures suites aux féminicides
france24fr.description: 🇿🇦 Après la découverte de 12 corps de femmes depuis mi-juillet dans un même secteur à l'Est de Johannesburg, Cyril Ramaphosa s’est adressé à la nation ce mardi. Le président sud-africain a annoncé un plan d’urgence contre les violences faites aux femmes.

france24fr.title: REPLAY : conférence de presse conjointe de Pedro Sanchez et Emmanuel Macron en Espagne
france24fr.description: Revivez la conférence de presse d’Emmanuel Macron et Pedro Sánchez à Madrid, le 30 septembre 2026, au terme de la visite d’État de deux jours du président français en Espagne.

nzz.description: Die GLP stellte sich zunächst hinter ein Verbot von Konversionstherapien im Kanton. Und änderte nun zweimal in kürzester Zeit ihre Meinung zum Thema.

nzz.description: Der Stadtrat will in finanziell schlechten Jahren auf den Zustupf an die städtischen Pendler verzichten. Die SP nennt dies «undemokratisch».

nzz.description: Eigentlich kam der Chihuahua Comando zur Armee, weil seine Besitzer ihn nicht mehr versorgen konnten. Nun wird er ausgebildet für eine mögliche Karriere als Suchhund. Er ist nicht der erste seiner Rasse in Uniform.

nzz.description: Der Rieter-Chef Thomas Oetterli schaffte es trotz grosser Machtfülle nicht, den Hersteller von Textilmaschinen aus der Krise zu führen. Peter Spuhler muss sich als Grossaktionär kritische Fragen gefallen lassen.

Pendant des décennies, la Suisse a prospéré grâce à un environne

letemps.title: Les canicules ne sont pas neutres: les femmes en paient le prix
letemps.description:
OPINION. De nombreuses études documentent le lien entre vagues de chaleur et violences domestiques, dont les femmes sont les premières victimes. Il est grand temps que les plans canicule cantonaux intègrent une analyse différenciée selon le sexe et le genre, écrit la conseillère nationale Martine Docourt (NE/PS)

Chaque été qui bat des records de chaleur, on nous répète que les personnes âgées

observador.title: Alfeite: Governo anuncia parceria entre idD e Fincantieri
observador.description: Nova joint venture entre a idD Portugal Defence e a Fincantieri vai gerir o estaleiro. Transição acontece ao longo de um ano, promete o Ministério da Defesa.

observador.title: Lisboa distingue Joaquim de Almeida e Marco Paulo
observador.description: A aprovação foi unânime, com os votos de PSD, IL, CDS-PP, PS, Livre, BE, PCP e Chega. As medalhas a Marco Paulo e Rogério Carvalho são atribuídas a título póstumo.

observador.title: CPI a mandatos de Luís Neves presidida por Chega
observador.description: A comissão de inquérito aos mandatos de Luís Neves como diretor da PJ foi aprovada com abstenção do PAN. Chega preside; PS e PSD assumem as vice-presidências.

observador.title: Rui Pinto vai sair do programa de proteção de testemunhas
observador.description: Rui Pinto vai deixar de beneficiar de medidas como a de residência em local secreto. Ainda não é certo se o hacker português também vai ficar sem proteção policial.

observador.title: Câmara de Lisboa falhou prazo para requalificar Martim Moniz
observador.description: Aprovada em 2022 e adjudicada em 2023, a requalificação da praça devia estar entregue em março de 2026. Está em outubro e ainda não começou.

observador.title: Federação de dadores alerta para problemas em Santarém
observador.description: Em 2024 e 2025 o número de dádivas desceu, e este ano a situação mantém-se. A falta de profissionais de saúde para recolha pode estar associado à baixa de dádivas.

observador.title: 21h. Ronaldo confirma saída do estágio da Seleção Nacional
observador.description: Numa publicação nas redes sociais, o capitão da seleção nacional diz que "a seu tempo" dirá a verdade sobre a saída. Ainda, Chega viabilizou as mudanças ao regime de arrendamento urbano.

observador.title: Paulo Serôdio: “Tenho todas as razões para desistir da ar...
observador.description: A celebrar 20 anos do atelier Orgânica, o arquitecto Paulo Serôdio acha que “a profissão do arquitecto está em extinção”, como diz Siza Vieira - graças a quem por pouco não ficou para a História…

observador.title: Suíça retira apoio à recandidatura de Infantino à FIFA
observador.description: A Associação Suíça de Futebol invoca falta de transparência e de credibilidade. Eleições à presidência da FIFA estão marcadas para março de 2027, em Rabat.

observador.title: Kremlin nega a existência de presos políticos na Rússia
observador.description: Posição que surge depois de ter sido noticiado que os EUA concordariam em aliviar as sanções económicas em troca da libertação de alguns desses prisioneiros.

observador.title: Rússia ameaça NATO com ataque nuclear
observador.description: Moscovo avisa que se a Aliança Atlântica tentar isolar o enclave russo de Kaliningrado, que faz fronteira com a Polónia e a Lituânia, a resposta do Kremlin será devastadora.

observador.title: Voo desviado. "Representa um escalar da ameaça"
observador.description: A especialista Ana Miguel dos Santos alerta que a violência extravasou para a aviação civil e que os avisos da Rússia à NATO aprofundam o dilema de segurança, elevando o risco de conflito.

observador.title: Drenagem. Túnel de Chelas parado já custou mais 4 milhões
observador.description: Obra do PGDL interrompida desde maio custa 15 mil euros por dia. Câmara admite que a tuneladora já estava parada antes dos achados arqueológicos em Chelas.

observador.title: PCP quer lares públicos e reforma aos 65 anos
observador.description: Dois projetos de lei apresentados na véspera do Dia do Idoso recuperam iniciativas chumbadas: 80 mil vagas em lares públicos até 2027 e fim do fator de sustentabilidade.

observador.title: PS propõe apoio mensal para universitários deslocados
observador.description: Complemento regional de alojamento estudantil abrangeria alunos que saem dos Açores para o continente, que se deslocam entre ilhas ou dentro da própria ilha.

observador.title: Moniz: plataformas devem identificar informação profissional
observador.description: Na conferência dos 40 anos da Lusa, José Eduardo Moniz alertou que os algoritmos tratam notícias e posts anónimos de forma igual. Google já marca conteúdos de IA.

observador.title: BE denuncia suspensão do programa de renda acessível jovem
observador.description: Na reunião do executivo desta quarta-feira, o BE exigiu transparência a Carlos Moedas sobre a paragem de casas do programa "De Volta ao Bairro". PS perguntou ainda se há intervenção do MP.

observador.title: Corpo de homem encontrado a boiar no rio Ave
observador.description: O alerta foi dado às 15h57 por um agricultor. O óbito foi declarado no local, sendo o corpo depois transportado para o Instituto de Medicina Legal do Porto. A identidade do homem não foi confirmada

spiegel.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Verlässt Portugals Nationalteam – Rücktritt offen
spiegel.description: Erst auf die Bank, dann die Abreise: Cristiano Ronaldo hat das Trainingslager der portugiesischen Nationalmannschaft verlassen. »Zu gegebener Zeit« will sich der 41-Jährige erklären.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Unabhängiges Onlineportal muss wegen angeblicher »LGBT-Propaganda« schließen
spiegel.description: Weil sie die »türkische Familienstruktur« schwächen könne, darf die Nachrichtenseite »T24« nicht länger berichten. Journalistenverbände sind entsetzt.

spiegel.title: AfD: Länder passen Beschlusspraxis aus Sorge vor Blockade an
spiegel.description: Aus Sorge vor einer Blockade durch die AfD ändern die Innenminister der Länder ihre jahrzehntelange Praxis: Künftig sollen Beschlüsse der Innenministerkonferenz auch gegen den Widerstand einzelner Länder möglich sein.

spiegel.title: AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt: Blufft Ulrich Siegmund bei der MP-Wahl?
spiegel.description: Ulrich Siegmund will im Dezember zum ersten AfD-Ministerpräsidenten Deutschlands gewählt werden. Die Rechtsextremisten behaupten, eine Mehrheit zusammenzuhaben. Stimmen muss das nicht.

spiegel.title: Ägypten: Sicherheitsapparat nimmt gesamte Redaktion von Faktencheck-Plattform »Matsada2sh« fest
spiegel.description: Bislang liegen wohl keine Angaben über den Ort der Haft oder deren Gründe vor: Ägyptische Behörden haben sechs Investigativjournalisten festgenommen – zwei davon auf offener Straße.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Mehr als 110 Verletzte bei Schulprotesten – 625 Festnahmen
spiegel.description: Die Lage an französischen Schulen eskaliert weiter: Nach Angaben der Regierung wurden über 600 Menschen festgenommen. Einige Personen haben Jugendliche offenbar gezielt zu Gewalt angestiftet.

spiegel.title: Wahlkampfhilfe für Donald Trump: USA wollen Europas Diesel-Vorräte freipressen
spiegel.description: Donald Trump steht vor den Zwischenwahlen mit dem Rücken zur Wand. Nun versucht er offenbar, die Europäer zur Freigabe ihrer strategischen Dieselreserven zu zwingen – um die Preise in den USA zu drücken.

spiegel.title: Irak: USA beenden Anti-IS-Militäreinsatz nach mehr als einem Jahrzehnt
spiegel.description: Die letzten US-Soldaten haben den Irak verlassen. Donald Trump prahlt zum Abschied von einem Sieg über die Terrormiliz »IS« und bezeichnet den Einsatz im Zweistromland als »Sumpf«.

spiegel.title: Marokko: König Mohammed VI. ernennt Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri zur erste Premierministerin
spiegel.description: Mohammed VI. macht weiter seine eigene Politik. Der marokkanische Monarch unterhält beste Beziehungen zu Israel und hat nun auch die erste Frau als Ministerpräsidentin eingesetzt – eine erfahrene Politikerin.

spiegel.title: Nato: Militärbündnis erhält Westfälischen Friedenspreis in Münster
spiegel.description: Das Verteidigungsbündnis wird in Münster für seinen Beitrag zur europäischen Friedensordnung ausgezeichnet. Bundeskanzler Merz hält die Laudatio, Nato-Generalsekretär Rutte nimmt den Preis entgegen.

spiegel.title: Israel-Gaza-Krieg: Kino-Start der umstrittenen Gaza-Doku »Naza«
spiegel.description: Im Dokumentarfilm »Naza« enthüllen israelische Soldaten die brutale Kriegsführung in Gaza. Israels Regierung wirft den Machern Landesverrat vor. Nun kommt der Film in die Kinos. Der SPIEGEL hat ihn gesehen.

spiegel.title: Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht BSW: Partei streicht Namen der Gründerin
spiegel.description: Das Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht streicht den Namen seiner Gründerin aus dem Parteinamen. Die Partei heißt ab dem 1. Oktober offiziell anders. Das Kürzel bleibt aber bestehen.

spiegel.title: Israel: Passagiere aus Flydubai-Maschine in Tel Aviv gelandet
spiegel.description: Ein Ersatzflug brachte sie an ihr Ziel: Die Israelis an Bord von Flug FZ1073 können vorerst aufatmen. Angehörige begrüßten sie in Tel Aviv mit Blumen und Luftballons.

spiegel.title: Bundestag: Linke-Abgeordnete Ferat Koçak gibt Sitz im Innenausschuss ganz auf
spiegel.description: In einer Stellungnahme räumte er einen »Fehler« ein: Der Bundestagsabgeordnete Ferat Koçak gibt nach Kritik an zu viel Nähe zu mutmaßlichen Angehörigen krimineller Clans seinen Sitz im Innenausschuss ganz auf.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Diese KI-Bosse waren ihm beim »Super Intelligence Luncheon« besonders nah
spiegel.description: Das Ergebnis der jüngsten KI-Runde in Washington ist mau. Doch US-Präsident Trump setzt auf Symbolik und starke Bilder. Das Schaulaufen der Tech-Elite in der Grafikanalyse.

spiegel.title: Tippfehler in Donald Trumps Abkommen für »Superintelligenz« sorgt für Spott
spiegel.description: »Vielleicht solltet ihr KI einsetzen, um solche Fehler zu erkennen«: In den sozialen Medien machen sich Nutzerinnen und Nutzer über einen Rechtschreibfehler in der vom Weißen Haus geteilten KI-Verordnung lustig.

spiegel.title: Liz Baffoe: »Lindenstraße«-Schauspielerin startet im neuen Job durch
spiegel.description: Nicht alle Schauspieler können von ihrer Arbeit leben. »Lindenstraße«-Schauspielerin Liz Baffoe hat daher jetzt einen Nebenjob gefunden.

spiegel.title: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Jäger erschießen drei Wildschweine in Swimmingpool
spiegel.description: Auf der Flucht vor Jägern sind drei Wildschweine in einen Swimmingpool geraten. Eine Rettung wäre zu gefährlich gewesen – deshalb erlegten die Jäger die Tiere in Absprache mit der Polizei.

nyt.title: Trump’s Voluntary A.I. Policing Echoes What Biden Did. But Is It Enough Today?
nyt.description: President Trump’s plan to let A.I. companies police themselves comes amid mounting examples that they are failing to put safeguards on the technology.

nyt.title: Congress Set to Leave Washington for the Midterms With No A.I. Progress
nyt.description: Senate Democrats blocked a measure that would encourage, but not require, states to protect consumers from power rate hikes tied to data center growth, and had no limits on A.I. use or deployment.

nyt.title: Who Attended Trump’s AI Luncheon, and Who Sat Where
nyt.description: A seating chart of the meeting illustrated growing divisions within the artificial intelligence industry and how it is viewed by the White House.

nyt.title: Panic and Heroics on FlyDubai Flight: ‘We Felt That This Was It’
nyt.description: A routine flight turned terrifying when a violent altercation broke out inside the cockpit and the aircraft dropped 17,000 feet in two minutes. Passengers subdued a knife-wielding attacker.

nyt.title: FlyDubai Flight to Israel Diverted After Clash Between Pilots: What We Know and Don’t Know
nyt.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel said one of the pilots may have been attempting to crash the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The plane landed in Saudi Arabia and all passengers were safe.

nyt.title: Democrats Block Stock-Trading Bill, Denying the G.O.P. a Pre-Midterm Win
nyt.description: A Republican measure to limit, but not bar, congressional stock trading faltered in the Senate as Democrats thwarted a G.O.P. bid to show progress on an issue that has rankled voters.

nyt.title: Becerra and Hilton to Face Off in Televised California Governor Debate
nyt.description: Xavier Becerra, a Democrat who served in the Biden administration, will debate Steve Hilton, a Republican former talk show host, in what’s likely to be their only face-off before the election.

nyt.title: Andrea Shaw Says Vaccines Killed Her Twins. Authorities Say She Suffocated Them.
nyt.description: In a small Idaho town, a young mother is accused of killing her young twins. She blames the childhood vaccines they received.

nyt.title: Fed’s Watchdog Finds No Misconduct or Illegal Activity in Costly Renovations
nyt.description: A new report by the Federal Reserve’s independent inspector general concluded that a nearly $2.5 billion construction project was poorly managed but made no referrals to the U.S. attorney general.

nyt.title: Justice Dept. Tries to Rebuke Federal Judges for Speaking to The Times
nyt.description: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz had warned that the administration’s actions “created a grave threat to the rule of law.” The attorney general accused him of “obvious bias.”

nyt.title: See How El Niño Is Washing Ashore in California
nyt.description: An enormous pulse of wave energy will soon reach Southern California and continue north, raising sea levels by half a foot and increasing threats from swells and tides.

nyt.title: Another Day of Pounding Rain Raises Flooding Fears in Texas
nyt.description: Texas had a dry summer, and rain on Wednesday could run off the arid ground like water on concrete.

nyt.title: Court Pauses Execution of Christa Pike, Tennessee’s Lone Woman on Death Row
nyt.description: Christa Pike tortured and murdered a classmate in 1995. She had been set to die on Wednesday, the first woman executed in the state in 200 years.

nyt.title: Google Wants Hollywood to Stop Being So Afraid of Technology
nyt.description: 100 Zeros, a collaboration between Google and Range Media Partners, aims to give the tech giant a foothold in movies, TV and emerging forms of entertainment.

nyt.title: Legal Immigrants Lose Medicaid Coverage Under Trump’s Bill
nyt.description: Many immigrants without green cards will no longer be eligible for the health insurance program for low-income people.

nyt.title: A Hasidic Jew Protested Against an Israeli Flag. He May Be Deported.
nyt.description: Yehonatan Ovadia, who opposed the mounting of the flag in a small New York town, belongs to a Hasidic branch that is anti-Zionist. He is now in ICE custody.

nyt.title: Salah Sarsour, Islamic Leader in Wisconsin, Can Be Deported, Judge Rules
nyt.description: Salah Sarsour, a vocal supporter of Palestinian rights who leads the state’s largest Islamic group, says the case is politically motivated and plans to appeal the decision.

nyt.title: D.A. in Cornell Case Hopes to Speak to Accuser as He Weighs New Evidence
nyt.description: District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said a woman’s report to the police in 2024 saying she had been raped at a fraternity did not support a criminal case. But he said he was now reaching out to her.

npr.title: Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps
npr.description: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.

npr.title: How Ukrainians are coping with new, more deadly Russian attacks
npr.description: Zanny Minton Beddoes, The Economist's editor in chief, just visited Ukraine. She says, despite all its drone weaponry, Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment, as Russia tries to make it unlivable.

npr.title: A pilot stabs another pilot and tries to crash their flight to Tel Aviv, Israel says
npr.description: As the plane went into a spin and began to plunge, a passenger and crew members got into the cockpit, subdued the pilot and diverted the flight to land in Saudi Arabia, Israel's leader says.

npr.title: U.S. forces exit Iraq amid Iran war. And, SCOTUS revives Trump deportation policy
npr.description: The U.S. has withdrawn its final troops from Iraq, leaving its defense future uncertain. And, the Supreme Court has sided for now with the Trump administration on third-country deportations.

npr.title: The U.S. military withdraws from Iraq over 2 decades after its invasion
npr.description: 23 years after the United States military invaded Iraq, sparking an insurgency and a civil war, the U.S. has withdrawn its forces, as the country still tries to combat Iranian influence.

npr.title: Retired general who led troops in Iraq warns U.S. exit may give Iran, ISIS an opening
npr.description: Retired Lt. Gen. H.R. McMaster, who commanded U.S. troops in Iraq, says the withdrawal could strengthen Iran and leave Iraq more vulnerable to ISIS.

npr.title: An 87-year-old woman whose eviction sparked protests in Spain is returning home
npr.description: María del Carmen Abascal's case has drawn tens of thousands of people to the streets in recent days and led the Spanish government to present measures to address the country's housing crisis.

npr.title: Potential Taiwan tension sparked 'last minute' change in Trump-Xi National Archives visit
npr.description: The sudden change was precipitated because of Chinese displeasure over one document that the U.S. had planned to show.

npr.title: Trump weakens fuel efficiency standards. And, Cornell fraternity rape case reopened
npr.description: The Trump administration has weakened fuel efficiency standards for new cars. And, prosecutors have reopened a Cornell University fraternity rape case.

npr.title: As the U.S. signals a smaller Middle East footprint, Turkey is ready to step in
npr.description: Turkey's bid for regional influence comes as the Middle East has been hit by profound shocks that started with the Hamas-led 2023 attack on Israel and continue with the seven-month-old war on Iran.

Mattarella emana il decreto legge sulla scuola
republika.description: Dal capo dello Stato via libera anche alla presentazione alle Camere del relativo disegno di legge di conversione

republika.description: L’ex campionessa olimpica di scherma è anche vicepresidente del Coni

republika.title: Ronaldo lascia il ritiro del Portogallo dopo le parole del ct Jesus: “Presto saprete la verità”
republika.description: Clima sempre più teso nella nazionale lusitana. L’allenatore: “Decido io chi gioca”. La rabbia di CR7

republika.description: Da una parte il deputato della Lega, dall’altra la senatrice di FdI. Il testo della norma non è stato scritto dal ministero di Urso. Ed è arrivato a Chigi senza quella norma. Una manina l’ha inserita dopo

republika.description: Il sospetto dirottamento del volo Flydubai è l’ultimo di una lunga serie di incidenti analoghi, molti dei quali per scopi terroristici. Dal primo della storia, quello del barone von Szilvas, fino all’azione in Francia per conoscere il terzo segreto di Fatima, ecco un elenco degli episodi più eclatanti

republika.title: Meloni scrive a von der Leyen: “A causa dell'inflazione serve più flessibilità”
republika.description: La premier in videocollegamento alla seconda edizione di "Oltre le Radici", l'evento annuale del quotidiano Il Gazzettino

republika.title: Dagli “eroi” ai motivi del dirottatore: i punti oscuri del dirottamento del volo Flydubai
republika.description: Perché l’aereo non ha puntato sullo Stato ebraico? Gli uomini che hanno sventato il presunto attentato erano agenti dei servizi di sicurezza israeliani in incognito? Sono alcune delle domande ancora senza risposta sul caso dell’aereo che andava da Dubai a Tel Aviv

republika.title: Scontro sui nuovi Cpr, Piantedosi ne vuole sei. Prorogato stop a Schengen con Spagna per 15 giorni
republika.description: Due in Trentino Alto Adige, uno in Calabria, Campania, Emilia Romagna e Toscana. Ecco dove saranno realizzati i nuovi centri per il rimpatrio

republika.title: Un testimone sul volo Dubai-Tel Aviv: “Abbiamo immobilizzato l’assalitore con i cavi delle cuffie”
republika.description: Tzvika Manes, ceo della Barak Capital Underwriting, era a bordo e ha raccontato alla televisione israeliana della colluttazione tra alcuni passeggeri e il presunto aggressore

republika.title: Gundogan: “In Guardiola ho visto il mio futuro. Yildiz straordinario, arriverà in alto”
republika.description: Il centrocampista tedesco ex City e oggi al Galatasaray si racconta a Repubblica, Die Zeit, The Guardian e Gazeta Wyborcza: “Klopp mi sbatté la porta in faccia per un ritardo, ma nessun allenatore è autentico come lui”

republika.title: Occhiuto punge Tajani: “Forse sua comunicazione andrebbe rivista, Forza Italia un po’ ingiallita”
republika.description: Il presidente della regione Calabria ha presentato il suo libro “Il coraggio di governare”

republika.title: Nasce il bonus carburante comunale. E’ ideato da un piccolo comune per combattere il caro prezzi
republika.description: Succede a Laurenzana (Potenza). Il contributo sarà destinato ai residenti in possesso della patente di guida e sarà modulato in base alla fascia di reddito

republika.title: Gli 84 minuti di terrore sul Flydubai per Tel Aviv: la ricostruzione attimo per attimo
republika.description: Accoltellamenti nella cabina di pilotaggio, una brusca perdita di quota e il codice 7500, che segnala un’”interferenza illecita a bordo”: il volo Flydubai diretto a Tel Aviv è stato fatto atterrare in emergenza a Tabuk, in Arabia Saudita. Mentre le autorità israeliane e saudite indagano, emergono le prime testimonianze dei passeggeri e l’ipotesi di un attacco terroristico

republika.title: Usa, sospesa a meno di un’ora dall’esecuzione la pena di morte per Christa Pike in Tennessee
republika.description: La 50enne doveva essere sottoposta a iniezione letale per un omicidio commesso a 18 anni. I giudici vogliono verificare se le denunce di stupri subiti dalla donna da bambina siano state prese in considerazione prima che venisse condannata

republika.title: Gaza, nuove testimonianze di soldati Idf dopo Naza: “Uccidere persone non sembrava più grave”
republika.description: Tre militari israeliani hanno raccontato al quotidiano spagnolo “El País” le esperienze vissute nella Striscia. Hanno deciso di parlare dopo le critiche al documentario esplose in Israele

republika.title: Sondaggi politici, Vannacci in maggioranza vale solo 2,2% ma è determinante per il premio
republika.description: La coalizione guidata da Meloni con Futuro nazionale supererebbe l'attuale 41,5%, soglia che non consente di ottenere il correttivo fissato dal Melonellum, arrivando insieme al partito dell’ex generale al 43,7%

republika.title: Balneari, il bando per le gare: concessioni fino a 20 anni, canone variabile e indennizzi
republika.description: Le istruzioni del Mit ai Comuni che dovranno procedere con le assegnazioni entro il 30 settembre 2027. Vincerà l’offerta più vantaggiosa, ai concessionari uscenti risarcimenti per gli investimenti effettuati negli ultimi 5 anni. Il canone allo Stato non sarà fisso

elpais.title: Un piloto apuñala a otro en pleno vuelo y pone al borde del desastre a un avión con destino a Israel
elpais.description: Los pasajeros y un miembro de la tripulación redujeron al agresor. El ministro israelí de Defensa denuncia un intento de “atentado yihadista” que pretendía estrellar el aparato, procedente de Dubái

elpais.title: Las imágenes del interior del avión: “Hemos controlado a los terroristas”
elpais.description: Un vídeo verificado por la agencia Reuters muestra a dos hombres heridos junto a pasajeros: “Necesitamos ayuda”

elpais.title: Un pasajero del vuelo de Dubái a Tel Aviv: “Até las manos al terrorista con unos auriculares”
elpais.description: Un piloto que iba a bordo evitó que la aeronave se estrellase: “Entró y enderezó la trayectoria”, relata un viajero del avión procedente de Dubái

elpais.title: El intento de secuestro de aviones vinculados a Israel, una amenaza que viene de los años setenta
elpais.description: Las milicias palestinas multiplicaron las tentativas hace medio siglo para exigir liberaciones de presos

elpais.title: Rusia amenaza con usar armas nucleares contra los países de la OTAN en plena escalada de tensión en el Báltico
elpais.description: Moscú ha advertido a la Alianza en una nota diplomática de que no debe intentar aislar Kaliningrado. La Alianza acusa a Moscú de usar una “retórica nuclear irresponsable”

elpais.title: La Aemet alerta de “peligro elevado” por un frente y una dana que afectarán de jueves a lunes al tercio oriental
elpais.description: Se trata de chubascos muy fuertes y persistentes que “pueden dar lugar a inundaciones locales súbitas y repentinas” en zonas bajas, arroyos y ramblas

elpais.title: El casero tendrá que indemnizar con 12 mensualidades al inquilino si decide no renovar el alquiler
elpais.description: El Ejecutivo retrasa un día la publicación en el BOE del segundo decreto de vivienda, que incluye la prórroga indefinida de los contratos y tendrá que votarse en el Congreso

elpais.title: ¿Cómo afectan los decretos de vivienda a los acampados en Sol?
elpais.description: Los manifestantes debaten sobre las medidas aprobadas en el Consejo de Ministros

elpais.title: Un dilema en Sol: cuándo parar

phys-org.description: A few days of rain do not change low groundwater levels after a long drought. phys-org.title: Clay tablets reveal how Babylonian students learned about their gods
phys-org.description: When it came to religious education in ancient Babylonia, in what is now Iraq, students had a lot to learn, ranging from the names of gods to their divine characteristics. A new study published in the journal Iraq has taken a deep dive into ancient texts and surviving clay tablets to find out just how these traditions were taught in the classroom.

phys-org.title: Some threatened species may miss out as zoos try to balance conservation efforts with competing pressures
phys-org.description: In the largest study of its kind, researchers at Nottingham Trent University analyzed more than 7,200 species across 613 zoos in 72 countries over a 30-year period. The team compared changes in zoo animal holdings with changes in species' conservation status, including extinction risk, international trade protections and involvement in zoo conservation breeding programs.

phys-org.description: A research team led by an Oregon State University scientist has demonstrated in a mouse model a potentially better way to care for women facing the life-threatening condition of ectopic pregnancy.

phys-org.description: Underwater archaeological investigations have been taking place in Lake Arendsee (Altmarkkreis Salzwedel) for several years. The discovery of Neolithic fish weirs, a high medieval barge (flat-bottomed cargo ship) and a late medieval dugout canoe attracted considerable attention.

phys-org.description: Schooling fish have long fascinated us with their mesmerizing collective movements and seemingly perfect coordination. But a new study on clonal mollies suggests that this behavior is not innate. During their first days of life, the fish still display distinct individual behaviors, and it is only around one month of age that they begin to form cohesive shoals, developing the coordinated movements characteristic of the group. phys-org.title: UV light locks radiation-detecting materials into durable, water-resistant films
phys-org.description: Florida State University researchers have developed a method to make a class of materials more robust and potentially easier to manufacture for advanced radiation detection devices, including those used in medical imaging and radiation therapy as well as space technologies.

phys-org.title: Stratospheric observatory Sunrise-III reveals intricate solar magnetic structures
phys-org.description: A team of researchers led by the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan discovered unexpectedly intricate magnetic structures above quiet-sun regions by observing the sun with the balloon-borne solar observatory Sunrise-III during its 2024 flight in Earth's stratosphere. The work is published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

phys-org.title: NASA satellite can monitor most of world's irrigation canals, study finds
phys-org.description: Irrigation canals form a sort of circulatory system for global agriculture. Across the world, millions of kilometers of human-made canals carry water from lakes, rivers and reservoirs downhill to farmland. Canals are vitally important to human food production, yet many agricultural areas lack the means to monitor the ebb and flow of water through these waterways. This forces farmers and water managers to rely on scattered gauges, inspections and local reports to make decisions about water use.

phys-org.title: Astronomers link mysterious cosmic flashes to collisions of dead stars
phys-org.description: For decades, astronomers have identified collisions between two neutron stars through bursts of gamma rays that can disappear in less than two seconds. But some of these violent encounters may also reveal themselves through X-ray flashes lasting several minutes. A new study published in Science Bulletin provides evidence for this connection, suggesting that merging neutron stars could be hiding among cosmic flashes whose origins have remained uncertain.

phys-org.title: How New World blackbirds conquered the Americas
phys-org.description: Where did the roughly 100 species of New World blackbirds alive today originate, and how did they spread across the Americas? Dr. Axel Arango Garcia and professor Chaitanya S. Gokhale from the Chair for Computational and Theoretical Biology (CCTB) at Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg (JMU) have reconstructed the evolutionary history of this family of birds.

phys-org.description: If your car's engine develops a stutter, that's generally a sign that you should go to a mechanic before it stops running. We tend to think the same way about our bodies: When something's broken, something bad usually follows. There might, however, be at least one exception to this rule.

phys-org.title: Bending nanoribbons tunes diamond's light emission without doping
phys-org.description: In a new Physical Review Letters study, researchers have demonstrated that bending diamond nanostructures can tune the light they emit without doping.

phys-org.title: AI-enhanced petitions on Change.org: More text, less success
phys-org.description: The change was obvious—but in the end, things stayed about the same. Cornell researchers took advantage of online petition website Change.org's gradual rollout of an artificial intelligence writing tool to gauge AI-enhanced language's impact on petition outcomes.

phys-org.title: New click beetle species named after Dominican Republic's Indigenous Arawak people
phys-org.description: A new species of click beetle with a glossy and highly domed black body has been described from cloud forest sites in the mountains of the Dominican Republic and named in honor of the Arawak peoples who lived on the island before European colonization.

phys-org.title: Research collaboration helps Gulf Coast communities plan for the unpredictable
phys-org.description: For communities along the Gulf Coast, hurricane season presents a recurring challenge: knowing when, where and how to evacuate before a major storm hits. To tackle this, researchers at Texas A&M University have spent more than a decade helping local, state and federal agencies develop clear, data-driven evacuation strategies.

phys-org.title: Mysterious oarfish's fins inspire large underwater robot design
phys-org.description: When designing a large underwater robot that could swim silently to avoid startling sea creatures, roboticist Rob Shepherd considered the unusual swimming system of oarfish, the meters-long fish whose ribbon-like dorsal fin moves in waves to propel its body.

undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

undark.title: Book Excerpt: Why the Brain Isn’t the Self
undark.description: The brain isn’t the self — consciousness is intimately linked with the human body. And if consciousness is the body’s way of knowing itself, then it is the living form in its entirety that should be taken as selfhood proper, with the brain as an especially feverish region.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
proj-syn.description: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.

proj-syn.title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
proj-syn.description: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

proj-syn.title: Is Another Eurozone Debt Crisis Looming?
proj-syn.description: At a time when the cost of servicing sovereign debt is rising globally, France stands out as an especially fragile case. Its public debt-to-GDP ratio is edging up toward that of Greece on the eve of its sovereign-debt crisis, and the French political system seems unable to do anything about it.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Reverse the Renminbi’s Rise?
proj-syn.description: In China, AI-driven productivity gains will most likely be in non-tradable services, which could push down relative prices and put downward pressure on the renminbi’s real exchange rate. To ensure that this does not also mean lower income and weaker demand, policymakers should ensure that the productivity dividend is broadly shared.

proj-syn.title: The Price of You
proj-syn.description: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data. AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.

proj-syn.title: Investing in Brain Health
proj-syn.description: Just as AI agents are mastering complex cognitive tasks, our own ability to perform the same tasks is eroding. Whether AI vindicates its boosters or fizzles out like the Metaverse craze of 2022, we will not fare well without a civilization-wide effort to rebuild the cognitive skills that make technological progress possible.

proj-syn.title: Europe Still Needs Molecules
proj-syn.description: Not even the most effective European electrification strategy will eliminate the need for the molecules that fossil fuels provide. Given this, Europe must diversify its oil and gas supplies, maintain its refining capacity, and lock in decarbonization by building a hydrogen-energy industry at scale.

proj-syn.title: Energy Security in an Age of Disruption
proj-syn.description: While there is no single prescription for energy security, strengthening “response capacity,” such as by establishing stockpiles, substituting sources, and diversifying suppliers, is essential. The point is not to eliminate vulnerabilities altogether, but to ensure that there are options when disruption arrives.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Common Currency-in-Waiting
proj-syn.description: While the phased approach of the Economic Community of West African States to implementing a long-delayed single currency will maintain momentum without compromising macroeconomic discipline, the bloc still lacks a robust mechanism to address asymmetric shocks. That is why fiscal integration must come first.

proj-syn.title: Learning to Reconcile
proj-syn.description: Political discourse in many Western countries has broken down, making it difficult for people with different viewpoints to live amicably with one another. The Reconciliation League, an international initiative by 13 universities and colleges, aims to train a generation of leaders who can change that.

proj-syn.title: Sheinbaum Is Just Another Trump Appeaser
proj-syn.description: After two years in office, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum continues to be widely praised, both in Mexico and abroad, for her handling of US President Donald Trump. But Sheinbaum has skillfully—and cynically—disguised the extent to which she has deferred to Trump on almost every issue.

proj-syn.title: Distorted Intelligence at the AI Frontier
proj-syn.description: The real problem for the frontier AI labs is not that their models are too powerful and already “misaligned” with the goals their creators set for them. Rather, it is that the models are being trained in ways that may be leading to a type of intelligence that will become less predictable.

proj-syn.title: Good Growth Requires the Right Public Finance
proj-syn.description: Although the Labour Party has done more to strengthen the United Kingdom's public-finance ecosystem in the past two years than any government in a generation, it must not stop there. If public investment is to meet its full potential, it must be reorganized to operate at scale on the public's behalf.

proj-syn.title: An EU–Canada Partnership Against Coercion
proj-syn.description: By proposing that the European Union and Canada begin work toward an association agreement, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has taken a critical first step toward establishing Europe as a hub for the world’s democratic middle powers. Such an arrange

proj-syn.title: The Opposing Forces Reshaping Global Finance
proj-syn.description: The financial industry is being pulled between two powerful forces: bottom-up financial technology is enabling seamless integration, while top-down geoeconomic statecraft is promoting fragmentation. So much for the conventional wisdom that finance will simply become smoother, cheaper, and more globalized over time.

proj-syn.title: The Dismally Obedient Science
proj-syn.description: While empirical inquiry has its place in economics, the pursuit of causality must not be allowed to displace the pursuit of explanation. Beyond identifying causal effects within existing arrangements, economists must investigate how those arrangements are produced, reproduced, and contested.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchy Is a Symptom, Not a Cause
proj-syn.description: The deepening political dysfunction plaguing the US can be traced not to wealth inequality, as some argue, but to the fact that different groups of voters believe different facts. A political strategy that takes this into account might eventually lead to wealth redistribution, but it must begin with improved critical-thinking skills.
